newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks pull gently back at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks pull gently back at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks surrendered early gains and closed a shade lower Friday in quiet trading as players snatched profits ahead of the weekend, dealers said.
"It's the typical Friday lull, with slack volume and weaker prices," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV eased 0.3 percent to 603.21, paring gains in the week to 4.1 percent, while the broad market dipped 0.1 percent.
Traders forecast the market would move sideways early next week as investors regroup.

"This is probably the time to realign in anticipation of a decline on Wall Street, which will test the bolsa's mettle," said Bonanno, noting the U.S. markets were probably headed for a technical pullback.

"Technical factors will come into play soon because the fundamentals are all very sound," said an analyst at a large local bank. "The U.S. long bond may have risen too much recently and may now pull us through a brief volatile patch."
Analysts predicted the MerVal would move between a floor of 595-600 points and a ceiling of 620 in the near term. The year's high of 615 was set last May.
Floor volume dwindled to 18.6 million pesos Friday from 28.4 million Thursday, while over-the-counter deals totaled 107.6 million pesos compared to 131 million Thursday.

Session losers beat winners 30 to 27 and 18 issues closed flat. Top main-tier gainers were petrochemical concern Indupa, which jumped 2.7 percent, gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur, which rose 0.8 percent, and oil giant YPF and agricultural holding firm Cresud, both up 0.6 percent.
Losers were led by oil firm Sol Petroleo and construction stock Polledo, off 4.2 percent and 1.9 percent, respectively.
